summary: Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff has led Trump endorsed Rep. Mike Collins in every recent public poll, including a 51 to 43 Trafalgar survey in early October cited by Newsweek, and Cook moved the race to Likely Democrat. Ossoff runs against Trump's tariffs, the Iran war and Medicaid cuts while attacking Collins over extremist associates and an ethics probe, and Collins casts Ossoff as a trust fund elite weak on the border.

issues.why: Ossoff says Democrats would repeal Trump's tariffs and end the Iran war he blames for high gas prices, while Collins says tariffs level the field with China.
Ossoff cites a hospital in Collins's district that closed its labor and delivery unit, and Collins points to $218 million in rural health funds.

issues.issue: Immigration and the Laken Riley Act
issues.why: Collins, the act's main author, blames Ossoff for weak border policy, while Ossoff says he backed the bill but opposes detaining people without criminal records.
Collins argues the war stopped Iran from getting a nuclear weapon, and Ossoff accuses Defense Secretary Hegseth of lying about it as service member deaths mount.
Ossoff highlights $531 million in federal aid for South Georgia farmers after Hurricane Helene.

storylines.title: Trump heads to Dalton
storylines.what: Trump planned a Friday stop in Dalton to campaign for Collins as PBS described Collins's fundraising as lackluster.

storylines.title: Republican mayor backs Ossoff
storylines.what: Valdosta Mayor Scott James Matheson, a Republican, is supporting Ossoff in a deeply conservative part of South Georgia.

storylines.title: Second debate turns bitter
storylines.what: Collins blamed Ossoff for Laken Riley's death and called it a race between Georgia and Georgetown, while Ossoff called Collins a Trump puppet and pressed him on an ethics probe and associates with Klan ties.

storylines.title: Ossoff leads in polls
storylines.what: A Trafalgar poll had Ossoff up 51 to 43, and Cook moved the race to Likely Democrat.

storylines.title: First debate gets personal
storylines.what: Ossoff said Collins brought dishonor to Georgia through personal bigotry, and Collins called Ossoff a trust fund kid who never had a job.

storylines.title: GOP doubts over Georgia
storylines.what: Some Republicans reportedly want to shift resources elsewhere, which the Collins campaign denies by pointing to Senate GOP ad buys over $1 million.

events.title: Laken Riley attack
events.prompt: The killing of nursing student Laken Riley is central to the immigration debate, and one side accuses the other of weak border policy. How does the campaign handle immigration?

opts.label: Condemn the detentions
opts.say: Stand by border security votes but condemn detaining people with no criminal records.

opts.label: Fentanyl and order
opts.say: Focus on fentanyl seizures and border staffing without talking about mass deportation.

opts.label: Full enforcement
opts.say: Tout the Laken Riley Act and back Trump's deportation push.

events.title: Tariffs on Georgia farms
events.prompt: Farmers in South Georgia are squeezed by tariffs and still recovering from Hurricane Helene. What is the campaign's trade message?

opts.label: Repeal the tariffs
opts.say: Promise to repeal Trump's tariffs and deliver more disaster aid to farmers.

opts.label: Targeted relief
opts.say: Seek tariff exemptions for farm inputs and push for Helene aid.

opts.label: Stand firm on China
opts.say: Defend tariffs as leveling the field with China and credit the tax cuts.

events.title: Ethics and extremism charges
events.prompt: One candidate faces a House ethics probe over use of government funds and questions about associates who posted antisemitic material. How does the campaign handle it?

opts.label: Press it hard
opts.say: Make the ethics probe and extremist ties a closing argument about character.

opts.label: Denounce and move on
opts.say: Denounce all hate clearly and return to kitchen table issues.

opts.label: Call it a smear
opts.say: Call the probe a politically motivated nothingburger and attack the opponent as an elite.

events.title: Medicaid cuts
events.prompt: Rural hospitals are closing services after federal Medicaid cuts in the 2025 tax law. What does the campaign promise?

opts.label: Reverse the cuts
opts.say: Promise to reverse the Medicaid cuts and push for full expansion.

opts.label: Rural fund
opts.say: Expand the rural health fund and protect labor and delivery units.

opts.label: Blame Obamacare
opts.say: Say the Affordable Care Act drove up costs and point to new rural funding.

debates.where: Atlanta Press Club at GPB, Atlanta

ads.theme: Ad buys over $1 million that the Collins campaign cites as proof national Republicans are still invested.

regions.name: Metro Atlanta core
regions.note: The Democratic base, where Ossoff needs heavy turnout among Black and suburban voters.

regions.name: Exurban Atlanta
regions.note: Fast growing suburbs that still lean Republican, with Henry trending Democratic.

regions.name: Collins's northeast Georgia base
regions.note: Collins's 10th District, deeply Republican apart from Athens.

regions.name: North Georgia mountains
regions.note: Trump country around Dalton, where he rallied for Collins.

regions.name: Middle and South Georgia
regions.note: Democratic cities like Savannah, Macon and Albany surrounded by rural Republican farm counties.
